blocks.markdown: The syllabus asks whether criminalizing the issuance of a bouncing check violates the **constitutional ban on imprisonment for debt**. The leading case is **Lozano v. Martinez**.

table.caption: Verbatim — 1987 Constitution, Article III, Section 20
rows: No person shall be imprisoned for debt or non-payment of a poll tax.

blocks.markdown: Simple explanation: the Constitution prevents imprisonment **merely because a person cannot pay a private debt**. B.P. Blg. 22 is treated differently: the punishable act is **issuing a worthless check under the law**, not simply failing to pay a debt. A civil debt may still exist, but the criminal case focuses on the statutory elements of the check offense.

table.caption: Exam takeaway: constitutionality
rows: Exam takeaway  When asked about constitutionality, state the distinction: debt non-payment versus the public-welfare offense of issuing a worthless check. Cite Lozano v. Martinez and the State’s police power.

description: Why BP 22 does not violate the ban on imprisonment for debt: Lozano v. Martinez.
title: Constitutionality
